paper.title: Optimal discovery with probabilistic expert advice

settings.name_in_paper: Optimal discovery with probabilistic expert advice (non-intersecting, uniform, equal-support experts; macroscopic limit)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Discovery problem with state-dependent rewards (an item counts only the first time it is found), equivalent to rested Markov arms; markovian environments are out of scope in the ontology. Guarantees are macroscopic-limit convergence statements, not regret bounds.
unmapped: Objective is the number of distinct interesting items discovered by time t (no reward for re-discovering an item), compared with the oracle closed-loop policy
Each expert draws i.i.d. from a fixed distribution P_i over a discrete set; analysis assumes non-intersecting supports on interesting items, supports of equal size N, uniform distributions
Macroscopic limit: N -> infinity with Q_i^N/N -> q_i in (0,1)
The analysed version of Good-UCB uses the support size N in its confidence bonus
settings.definition_quote: at each time step $t\in\N^*$, one picks an index $I_t\in\{1,\dots, K\}$, and one observes $X_{I_t, n_{I_t,t}}$ ... The goal is to choose the $(I_t)_{t\geq 1}$ so as to observe as many elements of $A$ as possible in a fixed horizon $t$ ... (i) non-intersecting supports ... (ii) finite supports with the same cardinality ... (iii) uniform distributions

symbols.F_lim: limiting proportion of interesting items found by the oracle closed-loop policy at normalized time t: F(t)=sum_i (q_i - T^{-1}(t))_+ with T(lambda)=sum_{i:q_i>lambda} log(q_i/lambda)
symbols.q_i: limit of Q_i^N/N, proportion of interesting items of expert i

conditions: all supports of size N, uniform distributions
Q_i^N/N -> q_i in (0,1) for all i
tuning: confidence bonus sqrt((2/n+1/N)^2 n log(2KN^4)/2) instead of c*sqrt(log t / n)

source.label: th:convUnifGUCB
source.quote: Assume that, for all $i\in\{1,\dots, K\}, Q^N_i/N$ converges to $q_i\in]0,1[$ as $N$ goes to infinity. Then, almost surely, the sequence of mappings $t\mapsto \Ft^N\left([Nt]\right)/N$ converges uniformly on $\R_+$ to the limiting proportion $F$ found during the same time by the oracle policy.

results.notes: Macroscopic optimality (convergence of the discovery curve to the oracle's), not a regret bound. Expression is the limit itself.

bound.regime: macroscopic limit N -> infinity, f^N/N -> phi

symbols.tau_lim: limiting normalized time needed by the oracle closed-loop policy to find a proportion phi of items: tau(phi)=T(L(phi))
symbols.phi: target proportion of interesting items found

conditions: all supports of size N, uniform distributions
Q_i^N/N -> q_i in (0,1) for all i

source.label: th:optGUCB
source.quote: In the macroscopic limit, $\taut^N(f^N)/N$ converges a.s. to the same limit $\tau(\phi)$ as for the oracle closed-loop policy when $f^N/N$ tends to $\phi$. Moreover, $\Ft^N(t^N)/N$ converges a.s. to the limiting proportion $F(t)$ found during the same time by the OCL policy when $t^N/N$ converges to $t$.

results.notes: Second part (pointwise convergence of discovered proportion) is subsumed by Theorem 2 (r1).
